title: DEFVERIFY: Do Hate Speech Models Reflect Their Dataset’s Definition?
benchmark_measurement: The paper's methodology (DEFVERIFY) measures the alignment between a hate speech dataset's definition and a trained model's behavior. In terms of religion, it specifically measures the accuracy of models in detecting hate speech targeted against various religious groups, using an enriched version of the HateCheck diagnostic dataset.
findings: The performance of models on detecting religion-based hate speech was highly dependent on the training dataset. For the Founta dataset, models recognized hateful content against religious groups but with many false positives. Models trained on the TalatHovy dataset, which were expected to perform well on religion, performed badly. In contrast, the model trained on the DGHS dataset performed well in identifying hate speech against religious groups. The HateXplain dataset was noted for explicitly including various religions (Buddhism, Christianity, Hinduism, Islam, Judaism) in its definition.
